item.text: Both ads are delivering. The first check shows $55.87 spent and 7 link clicks; that’s too little data to favor either post yet. I’ll keep the test running and check again this evening.

The double-feature post has 17 link clicks at $6.50 each; the pricing post has 9 at $10.35 each. I’ll shift roughly two-thirds of the budget toward the double-feature post while retaining the pricing test. This is a click-cost decision; trial performance remains unknown.
Spend is $252.04 for 34 link clicks. The double-feature post still has the lower cost per click, and both groups remain within their caps. I’ll keep the current allocation for the next check.

The double-feature post has 34 clicks at $6.12 each, versus 11 at $10.14 for the pricing post. Delivery is below pace, so I’ll raise daily allowances and move the lifetime allocation to $760/$190 in favor of double features. The combined hard cap stays $950.
Spend is now $493.15 for 76 link clicks. The double-feature post’s cost per click has improved to $5.79, so I’ll retain the current allocation and continue monitoring through Thursday.

The campaign has spent $655.77 and generated 108 link clicks. Double features continues to lead on click cost. Both ads are scheduled to end at midnight Eastern after Thursday, with $294.23 remaining under the total cap.
At Thursday’s midday check, spend is $789.81 with 137 link clicks. The combined lifetime caps leave at most $160.19 available for the rest of the flight.
The evening check shows $873.16 spent and 156 link clicks. I’ll let the scheduled flight finish, then pause the campaign and pull the closing totals.

Completed November 30–December 3, Eastern time. Campaign is now paused.

- Spend: **$936.85** of $950
- Impressions: **330,442**
- Link clicks: **168**

Shifted budget toward the double-feature post for its lower click cost. Trial starts remain unverified; they require your signup records.
